## Editorial pass 2026-08-29

Clear premise and audience. It is also the fastest-rotting piece on the board, and that should shape how it is written.

**1. Write it so it degrades gracefully.** This is built entirely on prices, quota buckets, and plan structures across Antigravity, Cursor, and Grok Bot — every one of which will change. The idea already says recheck before publish. Stronger version: **put the durable principle in the prose and quarantine the volatile numbers in a clearly dated table.** Then when the plans move, one table is stale instead of the whole article. Without that, this piece is wrong within a month and stays wrong.

**2. The title is a rule; the article should teach the reason.** "Never Use Fast" is a good hook and a bad thesis if left unexplained. The actual argument is *you are buying latency you do not need with tokens you do.* A reader who learns the reasoning can re-derive the answer when the plans change. A reader who only learns the rule is stranded the moment it stops being true.

**3. Companion discipline.** It is the how-to for "Maximize Value, Not Intelligence." Link the parent, do not re-argue it.

**Verification, deliberately late.** The Anth.us repo already carries a committed claim that Grok Bot quota is calendar-month aligned rather than billing-cycle aligned — exactly the kind of specific, checkable, short-lived fact this piece runs on. Do the pricing and quota sweep as **late as possible** before publish. Doing it now is wasted work; it will need redoing.

**Research: yes, but not yet.** Schedule the sweep against the publish date, not against today.
